reason: Judged only the gate claim (another refuter judges undo itself). It holds, and I proved it two ways. (1) Read: interaction-check.mjs lines 320-340 are the ONLY undo assertions in the file; the block opens a fresh owner-editing page, never moves anything, and reads five purely structural facts off one probe object — element present, count===1, role="status", a Ctrl Z, no script on the page at all and the button DISABLED — passes all five (exists/one/live/control/says all true). On the real master the same five read identically before any move, after three real +7 moves (item top 322 -> 616, sentence still 'the invitations moved seven days closer'), and after clicking Undo and pressing Ctrl+Z (top 616 -> 616). The gate's verdict is invariant to whether the surface tells the truth, whether its control is even enabled, and whether anything is reversible. It also cannot fail on the exact defect it was written for: lessons.md 'Nothing reversible' is guarded here by shape only, so the class returns in its subtler form — the surface exists, and does nothing — and the gate certifies it. This is the opposite of restating what automation proves; it shows this automation proves nothing here.
sharpenedFix: Fix aimed at the right file, but three corrections before it is written. (a) 'no .b-undo exists before any move' directly contradicts the existing assertion 'a reversibility surface exists', which runs on a fresh owner-editing page and would start failing. Restructure the block instead of appending to it: on one page, assert absence first, perform a real move, then run the five structural assertions AFTER the move — the shape checks are fine, they are just being run at the wrong moment. (b) Drop 'its date' from the restore list, or it fails against a correct undo: move() rewrites .b-stepRead to 'in N days' and permanently drops the longYear date the pre-move readout carried (render-b.js line ~236), and .b-away is a deliberate bare number. Name the real observables instead: item.offsetTop, item.dataset.away, .b-away textContent, .b-stepRead textContent, and the item's accessible name. (c) Add the two cheap assertions that an inert prop cannot survive, which the fix as written omits: the sentence must CHANGE between two different moves (move item A, capture the text, move item B, assert the text differs and names B), and the Undo button must not be disabled and must be reachable by Tab. Then assert both paths independently — the button click and a Cmd/Ctrl+Z keydown each restore all five observables, and focus lands back on the .b-step that made the change.
